MG21.analysis: WD-40 penetrates rust and frees links; gloves protect hands; screwdriver can pry; dry lube for after. Carabiner and scissors not useful. Useful: WD-40, gloves, screwdriver, dry lubricant.
MG21.final:
step1: Spray WD-40 on the rusted chain and wait a few minutes.
step2: Wearing gloves, flex the links by hand, using the screwdriver to pry stiff links loose.
step3: Loop the chain over the rear sprocket and chainring, pry it onto teeth with the screwdriver, turn pedal.
step4: Apply dry lubricant.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG22.analysis: Brush: long reach, can push the toy. Step ladder: height. Rocking chair unstable; hanger can't hook fuzz; strap and broom optional. Useful: ladder, long-bristled brush (or broom).
MG22.final:
step1: Set up the step ladder beside the wardrobe.
step2: Climb and use the long-bristled brush (or wicker broom) to sweep or push the toy toward the edge until it falls.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG23.analysis: Pot, bottle allow boiling and bandana filters sediment, but chemical contamination from agriculture is not removed by boiling or cloth; boiling can concentrate chemicals. No chemical filter, charcoal, or distillation setup with condenser of enough quality.
MG23.final:
Not possible: boiling and cloth filtering remove germs and particles, not agricultural chemicals, and no listed item can adsorb or reliably distill them out.
VERDICT: UNSOLVABLE

MG24.analysis: Items offer observation or filtering only. DNA extraction needs detergent, salt, and alcohol, none available. Coffee filter only filters; nothing to lyse cells or precipitate DNA.
MG24.final:
Not possible: no lysis agent (detergent), salt, or cold alcohol is provided, so DNA cannot be released or precipitated with only filters, a beaker, and bags.
VERDICT: UNSOLVABLE

MG25.analysis: Foam inserts and moleskin are good; felt pads fill space; tissue paper fills; rubber bands weak; double-sided tape weak. Useful: foam inserts, moleskin, felt pads.
MG25.final:
step1: Place foam inserts (or felt pads) inside the shoes under the heels/insoles to take up extra volume.
step2: Stick moleskin pads on the heel interior to add grip and stop slipping.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG26.analysis: T-shirt can be torn into strips (scissors dull but can nick fabric then tear); gloves help; ladder reaches 6ft+ person reach, so tie accessible parts. Watering can, soil useless.
MG26.final:
step1: Use the scissors to nick the t-shirt and tear it into long strips; twist or double strands for strength.
step2: Stand on the ladder wearing gloves and tie the vines to the trellis with the strips, as high as the ladder reaches, then train vines upward later.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG27.analysis: Bandanas are sturdy cloth for bundles; pantyhose weak but usable inside bandanas or as ties; stapler, frame, nail polish, knife, compass not needed.
MG27.final:
step1: Lay out each bandana and pile Legos in the center.
step2: Gather corners, knot them to make sacks; use pantyhose legs as extra ties or inner liners (Legos inside bandana).

MG28.analysis: Paper is straight-edged with known standard size; pen/pencil to mark; clip or stapler to hold. Keyboard useless, others not needed.

step2: Mark and number the divisions with a pen on a strip of paper, or fold the strip to subdivide into centimeters.

MG29.analysis: Broom reaches only partly alone; sturdy chair adds height; stand on chair and bat the lightweight toy with the broom. Cookie sheet, mirror, keys, string not needed.

step2: Stand on the chair and hold the straw broom by the handle end, then nudge the toy until it falls off.
step3: Catch it, or let it drop onto a cushion.
